newsitem.title: GERMANY: German media watchdog bemoans TV bottleneck.
newsitem.headline: German media watchdog bemoans TV bottleneck.

text.p: The current bottleneck in analogue television broadcasting capacity is unbearable, Norbert Schneider, director of the broadcasting commission (LfR) of the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia said on Monday.

Schneider said that both the state media authorities and the television broadcasters were not prepared to put up with the lack of broadcasting space any longer, and criticised Deutsche Telekom's role as broadcast-space provider.
"It is a scandal that the monopoly-holder Telekom does nothing to alleviate the shortage of broacast space," said Schneider.
Schneider suggested opening up the S2 and S3 channels for television, which were currently taken up with radio programming.
The LfR said that it would broadcast the children's channel Nickelodeon and the English-language channel NBC Europe alternately on the same cable frequency.
The public children's channel Kinderkanal would now be sent out alternately with the French-German joint-venture arte, using the broadcasting capacities previously used by Nickelodeon.
The European Business News (EBN) channel will now be broadcast alongside the sports channel Eurosport, using nighttime broadcast periods not used by Eurosport.
The LfR went on to say that two Belgian channels, the Flemish-speaking BRT1 and the French-speaking RTBF1 would be available in the Aachen region.
